fk: 이렇게 늦게 갈 바에야 차라리 안 가는 게 좋아요.
fe: Rather than go this late, it's better not to go at all.
xk: 동사 뒤에 붙어요. 'A를 할 거라면 차라리 B가 나아요'라는 뜻이에요. 앞의 일이 마음에 안 들 때 써요.
xe: Attach it to a verb stem. It means 'if you're going to do A, B is better.' Use it when you dislike A.
nk: 뒤에는 '차라리'나 '-는 게 좋아요'가 자주 와요. 앞에는 싫은 선택, 뒤에는 덜 나쁜 선택이 와요. '-느니'보다 조금 더 차분하고 글에도 써요.
ne: The second part often has 차라리 or -는 게 좋아요. The first part is the choice you dislike; the second is the lesser evil. It sounds calmer than -느니 and also works in writing.
ex: 비싼 호텔에서 잘 바에야 차라리 친구 집에서 자는 게 좋아요.
Rather than sleep in an expensive hotel, it's better to sleep at a friend's place.
돈을 빌릴 바에야 안 사는 게 좋아요.
Rather than borrow money, it's better not to buy it.
혼자 고민할 바에야 친구한테 물어보는 게 좋아요.
Rather than worry alone, it's better to ask a friend.
참고 일할 바에야 그만두고 쉴 거예요.
Rather than put up with it and work, I'll quit and rest.
냉장고를 고칠 바에야 새것을 사는 게 좋아요.
Rather than fix the fridge, it's better to buy a new one.
cz: 친구와 ___ 차라리 먼저 사과하는 게 좋아요. (싸우다, -(으)ㄹ 바에야)
Rather than fight with a friend, it's better to apologize first.
숙제를 ___ 지금 빨리 끝내는 게 좋아요. (미루다, -(으)ㄹ 바에야)
Rather than put off the homework, it's better to finish it quickly now.

fk: 공짜면 몰라도 이 가격에는 안 사요.
fe: If it were free, maybe, but I won't buy it at this price.
xk: 앞에 조건을 말해요. 그 조건이라면 괜찮을 수 있지만, 아니면 안 된다고 말해요.
xe: Name a condition first. If that condition were true it might be fine, but otherwise it isn't.
nk: 뒤에는 보통 '안 해요', '못 해요', '싫어요'가 와요. 지금은 그 조건이 아니라는 뜻이 숨어 있어요. '-더라도'는 '그래도 한다'는 뜻이라서 달라요.
ne: The second part is usually negative: won't, can't, don't like. It hints that the condition isn't true now. -더라도 means 'even so, I'll do it', so it is different.
ex: If it were on sale, maybe, but I won't buy at full price.
친구면 몰라도 모르는 사람에게는 못 빌려줘요.
I might lend it to a friend, but not to a stranger.
집이 가까우면 몰라도 매일 가는 건 힘들어요.
If it were close, maybe, but going every day is hard.
월급이 많으면 몰라도 이 일은 하고 싶지 않아요.
If the pay were high, maybe, but I don't want to do this job.
하루 이틀이면 몰라도 한 달은 못 참아요.
A day or two, maybe, but I can't stand a month.
cz: 주말에 ___ 평일에는 일이 많아서 못 가요. (한가하다 + -(으)면 몰라도)
Weekends, maybe, if I'm free, but I can't go on weekdays because of work.
시간이 ___ 오늘은 바빠서 못 가요. (많다 + -(으)면 몰라도)
If I had lots of time, maybe, but I'm busy today, so I can't go.

fe: If I eat it, I'm full; if I throw it away, it feels wasteful.
xk: 동사 뒤에 붙어요. '이렇게 하려고 하니 이게 걸리고, 저렇게 하려고 하니 저게 걸려요'라는 뜻이에요.
xe: Attach it to a verb stem. It means 'if I try A, there's a problem; if I try B, there's a problem too.'
nk: 보통 둘을 짝지어서 말해요. 둘 다 어렵거나 마음에 안 드는 처지예요. 하나만 쓰면 어색해요.
ne: Usually used as a pair. You are stuck: both options have a problem. A single -자니 alone sounds odd.
ex: 일을 그만두자니 돈이 걱정이고, 계속하자니 너무 힘들어요.
If I quit, I worry about money; if I keep going, it's too hard.
이 옷을 입자니 작고, 저 옷을 입자니 커요.
If I wear this, it's small; if I wear that, it's big.
친구를 부르자니 늦었고, 혼자 가자니 무서워요.
If I call a friend, it's late; if I go alone, it's scary.
전화하자니 바쁠 것 같고, 문자를 보내자니 급해서 걱정이에요.
If I call, they may be busy; if I text, I worry because it's urgent.
병원에 가자니 시간이 없고, 그냥 쉬자니 아파요.
If I go to the hospital, I have no time; if I just rest, it hurts.
cz: If I stay home and play, it's boring; if I go out, it's cold.
이 가방을 ___ 무겁고, 놓고 가자니 불안해요. (들다)
If I carry this bag, it's heavy; if I leave it, I feel uneasy.

fe: I'd rather walk than take a taxi.
xk: 동사 뒤에만 붙어요. 'A를 하느니 차라리 B를 해요'라는 뜻이에요. A가 정말 싫다는 느낌이에요.
xe: Only attaches to verbs. It means 'I'd rather do B than A.' You really dislike A.
nk: 말할 때 자주 써요. '-(으)ㄹ 바에야'보다 감정이 더 강해요. 뒤에는 '차라리'와 '-는 게 좋아요'가 자주 와요. 형용사에는 못 붙어요.
ne: Common in speech and stronger in feeling than -(으)ㄹ 바에야. Often followed by 차라리 or -는 게 좋아요. It can't attach to adjectives.
ex: 남을 기다리느니 내가 직접 하는 게 좋아요.
I'd rather do it myself than wait for someone else.
비싼 밥을 먹느니 집에서 해 먹는 게 좋아요.
I'd rather cook at home than eat an expensive meal.
늦게 가서 혼나느니 차라리 일찍 일어나는 게 좋아요.
I'd rather get up early than arrive late and get scolded.
싸게 팔느니 그냥 친구한테 줄 거예요.
I'd rather just give it to a friend than sell it cheap.
I'd rather save money than waste it.
cz: 길을 ___ 차라리 사람들에게 물어보는 게 좋아요. (헤매다, -느니)
Rather than wander around lost, it's better to ask people.
인터넷에서 ___ 차라리 직접 가서 보는 게 좋아요. (찾다, -느니)
Rather than search online, it's better to go and see it yourself.

fe: Wow, it snowed a lot!
xk: 지금 새로 알게 된 사실에 가볍게 놀랄 때 써요. 동사는 '-는걸요', 형용사는 '-(으)ㄴ걸요', 과거는 '-았/었는걸요'예요.
xe: Use it when you notice something new and are lightly surprised. Verb: -는걸요. Adjective: -(으)ㄴ걸요. Past: -았/었는걸요.
nk: 혼잣말처럼 말하거나 가까운 사람에게 말할 때 자연스러워요. '-네요'와 비슷한데, '-는걸요'는 놀람과 함께 '생각과 달라요'라는 느낌이 조금 더 있어요. '재미있다·맛있다·멋있다·없다'처럼 '있다/없다'로 끝나는 형용사는 '-는걸요'가 붙어요(재미있는걸요). '요'를 빼면 반말이라서, 윗사람에게는 '요'를 꼭 붙여요.
ne: Natural as a half-to-yourself remark or with someone close. Similar to -네요, but -는걸요 adds a bit of 'this is not what I expected'. Adjectives ending in 있다/없다 (재미있다, 맛있다, 멋있다, 없다) take -는걸요, as in 재미있는걸요. Without 요 it is casual speech, so keep the 요 when you talk to someone older.
ex: This coffee is stronger than I thought.
The prices in this shop are really cheap!
Yuna, your room is so big.
Wow, the sea is really beautiful!
Oh, the rain has already stopped.
마이크 씨는 매운 음식도 잘 먹는걸요.
Mike, you eat spicy food well too!
cz: Oh, this book is really interesting!

fe: It's a bit late now, you know.
xk: 상대 말에 부드럽게 이유를 대며 다른 생각을 말할 때 써요. 만드는 법은 감탄할 때와 같아요.
xe: Use it to gently give a reason that goes against what the other person said. It is formed the same way as the surprise use.
nk: '안 돼요'처럼 딱 잘라 말하지 않고 '사실은 이래요' 하고 부드럽게 말해요. 거절이나 반대를 약하게 할 때 좋아요. 아주 격식 있는 자리에서는 잘 안 써요.
ne: Instead of a flat 'no', it says 'actually, it's like this' in a soft way. Good for a mild refusal or disagreement. Not used in very formal situations.
ex: That movie has already finished, you know.
The shop is closed today, actually.
I can't eat spicy food, you see.
I've already read that book, though.
There are too many people right now, you know.
서연 씨는 오늘 회사에 안 오는걸요.
Seoyeon isn't coming to the office today, actually.
cz: Actually, I can't swim, you know.
Actually, that shop is closed on Mondays, you know.

f: N 받침 없음+라면 · N 받침 있음+이라면
fe: When it comes to cooking, I'm confident.
xk: '그것에 관해서라면'이라는 뜻이에요. 명사 뒤에 붙여서 그 일이 가장 잘하는 것이라고 강조해요. 받침이 있으면 '이라면', 없으면 '라면'이에요.
xe: It means 'as for that thing'. Put it after a noun to stress that this is the area you are best at. After a final consonant: 이라면. Without: 라면.
nk: 뒤에 '잘해요, 최고예요, 자신 있어요'처럼 자신이나 칭찬하는 말이 자주 와요. 'N은/는'보다 '그것만큼은'이라는 느낌이 강해요. '만약 N이라면'(조건)과 모양이 같아서 문장 뜻으로 구별해요.
ne: It is often followed by words of confidence or praise, like 'I'm good at it' or 'it's the best'. Stronger than N은/는: 'at least when it comes to that'. It looks the same as the 'if it is N' form, so use the sentence meaning to tell them apart.
ex: When it comes to singing, Minsu is the best.
If it's Korean food, I like anything.
For value for money, this shop is the best.
If it's about good restaurants, ask Seoyeon.
As for computers, Hajun knows them well.
cz: When it comes to cars, Dohyun knows the most.
As for games, my younger sibling is the best.

fe: Even if you post nasty comments, would you really feel better?
xk: '아무리 해도 소용없다'를 질문 꼴로 강하게 말해요. 앞에 -(으)ㄴ들, 뒤에 -겠는가를 써요. 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ들, 있으면 -은들, 명사는 N인들이에요.
xe: This says 'it is no use, however much you do it' in the form of a question. Use -(으)ㄴ들 in the first part and -겠는가 at the end.
nk: 답을 바라는 질문이 아니에요. 글이나 연설에서 '그렇지 않다'는 주장을 강하게 말할 때 써요. 뒤에는 꼭 -겠는가 같은 반문이 와야 해요. -더라도는 '그래도 괜찮다'는 말도 되지만, -(으)ㄴ들은 늘 '소용없다'는 뜻이에요.
ne: It is not a real question; it is a strong claim that the opposite is true. It is used in writing and speeches, and the end must be a rhetorical question like -겠는가. -더라도 can lead to many outcomes, but -(으)ㄴ들 always means 'it is no use'.
ex: 인기가 많은들 팬덤이 떠나면 무슨 소용이겠는가.
Even if you are popular, what good is it once your fandom leaves?
아무리 논거가 좋은들 듣는 사람이 없으면 누구를 설득할 수 있겠는가.
However good your arguments are, whom can you persuade if no one listens?
겉모습만 화려한들 속내가 비어 있으면 누가 믿겠는가.
Even if it only looks fancy, who would trust it if the inside is empty?
Even if you are rich, would you be happy if you are stuck in vanity?
지금 서두른들 이미 늦은 일을 되돌리겠는가.
Even if you hurry now, can you undo what is already too late?
cz: 아무리 크게 ___ 아무도 듣지 않는데 무슨 소용이겠는가. (소리치다 + -(으)ㄴ들)
However loudly you shout, what use is it when no one is listening?
Even if that person apologizes now, who would forgive them?

fe: Why does a fandom grow this fast?
xk: 글에서 독자에게 문제를 던지는 질문이에요. 동사는 -는가, 형용사는 받침이 없으면 -ㄴ가, 있으면 -은가를 써요.
xe: A written question that raises an issue for the reader. Use -는가 with verbs and -(으)ㄴ가 with adjectives.
nk: 글·칼럼·연설에서 써요. 말할 때는 -나요?, -어요?를 더 많이 써요. 답을 바로 듣고 싶은 게 아니라 같이 생각해 보자는 뜻이 커요.
ne: Used in essays, columns and speeches. In conversation people say -나요? or -어요? instead. It invites the reader to think, not to answer right away.
ex: Why do people look for provocative videos?
How do nasty comments hurt people?
Why is jumping to conclusions dangerous?
What does vanity leave us with?
cz: 학생들은 왜 시험 전에만 열심히 ___ (공부하다, 글 질문)?
Why do students study hard only before exams?

fe: Is happiness money?
xk: 글에서 명사에 대해 묻는 질문이에요. 명사 뒤에 -인가를 붙여요. 받침이 있어도 없어도 같아요.
xe: A written question about a noun. Add -인가 after the noun, with or without a final consonant.
nk: 'N이에요?'의 글말 꼴이에요. 둘 중에 고르는 질문(N인가, N인가?)에도 자주 써요. 문제를 던져서 독자가 다시 생각하게 해요.
ne: This is the written form of 'N이에요?'. It is often used to pose a choice between two things. It makes the reader stop and rethink.
ex: Is the real problem technology or people?
Is the Korean Wave just a passing trend?
Is this the future we wanted?
cz: Is the purpose of school only grades?

fe: You want me to come at six tomorrow morning?!
xk: 상대가 시킨 말이 믿기지 않거나 어이없을 때 되물어요. 받침이 없으면 -라니요, 있으면 -으라니요예요.
xe: Use it to push back when you can't believe what someone told you to do. -라니요 after a vowel, -으라니요 after a final consonant.
nk: 놀람과 불만, '못 하겠다'는 마음이 들어 있어요. 단순히 다시 확인하는 '-(으)라고요?'보다 훨씬 세요. 윗사람에게 쓰면 버릇없게 들릴 수 있어요.
ne: It carries surprise, complaint, and a hint of 'no way I'll do that.' It is much stronger than the plain double-check -(으)라고요?. To a superior it can sound rude.
ex: 이 많은 일을 오늘 다 끝내라니요?
You want me to finish all this work today?!
You expect me to eat all this spicy food?!
이 밤에 혼자 가라니요, 저는 무서워요.
Go alone at this hour of the night? I'm scared.
이 큰 케이크를 혼자 만들라니요? 저는 요리도 못해요.
Make this big cake by myself? I can't even cook.
시험 전날에 놀라니요? 저는 공부해야 해요.
Play the day before the exam? I have to study.
The flight time has passed and you tell me to wait?!
cz: 저한테 이렇게 어두운 방에서 책을 ___ (읽다)? 믿을 수 없어요.
You're telling me to read in a room this dark? I can't believe it.
저한테 이 추운 날에 찬물에서 ___ (수영하다)? 안 돼요.
You're telling me to swim in cold water on a day this cold? No way.

fe: You want to go see a movie at this hour?!
xk: 상대가 '같이 하자'고 한 말이 믿기지 않을 때 되물어요. 받침 상관없이 어간에 -자니요를 붙여요.
xe: Use it when someone's 'let's do it' sounds unbelievable. Attach -자니요 to the verb stem, with or without a final consonant.
nk: '왜 지금 그걸 해요?' 하는 놀람과 거절의 느낌이 있어요. 친한 사이에서 많이 써요. 제안을 그냥 다시 묻는 '-자고요?'보다 감정이 세요.
ne: It expresses shock and refusal, as in 'why would we do that now?' It is common between close people. It is stronger in feeling than the plain double-check -자고요?.
ex: It's raining this hard and you want to climb a mountain?!
We have no money and you want to buy an expensive bag?!
We just ate and you want to eat again?!
Walk there carrying all this luggage?!
cz: 아직 일이 많은데 같이 ___ (퇴근하다)? 저는 못 가요.
I still have lots of work, and you want us to leave together? I can't go.
시험 전날인데 우리 같이 ___ (여행하다)? 말도 안 돼요.
It's the day before the exam and you want us to travel together? That's ridiculous.

fe: Of course I'll help with that!
xk: 상대의 말이나 질문에 '당연하죠!' 하고 강하게 대답해요. 동사·형용사는 어간에 -고말고요, 명사는 N(이)고말고요를 써요.
xe: Answer someone's question or statement with a strong 'of course!' Use -고말고요 on verb or adjective stems and N(이)고말고요 on nouns.
nk: 받침이 있어도 없어도 형태가 같아요. 힘을 주어 확실하게 동의하는 말이에요. 친한 사이에서 많이 쓰고, 끝의 '요'로 높임을 나타내요. 지난 일은 -았/었고말고요예요. 단순한 대답 '네'보다 마음이 많이 들어가요.
ne: The form is the same with or without a final consonant. It gives firm, emphatic agreement and is warm in tone; the final 요 makes it polite. For past events use -았/었고말고요. It carries much more feeling than a plain 'yes.'
ex: This place's kimchi stew? Of course it's delicious.
Yes, of course I'll keep my promise.
Do I know him? Of course. He was our teacher.
Of course that person is our teacher.
Will I eat? Of course. I'm really hungry.
Expensive? Of course it is. This bag costs a million won.
cz: 오늘 저녁에 올 거예요? 그럼요, 꼭 ___ (오다).
Are you coming tonight? Of course, I'll definitely come.
이 일을 끝낼 수 있어요? 그럼요, 제가 ___ (끝내다).
Can you finish this work? Of course, I'll finish it.

fk: 비라도 그치면 소풍을 갈 수 있으련만.
fe: If only the rain would stop, we could go on a picnic.
xk: 지금은 그렇지 않지만 '그러면 좋을 텐데' 하는 아쉬운 마음을 말해요. 받침이 없으면 -련만, 있으면 -으련만을 붙여요.
xe: Expresses regret that things are not the way you'd wish: 'it would be nice if…, but it isn't so'. Add -련만 after a vowel and -으련만 after a consonant.
nk: 일상 대화에서는 -(으)면 좋겠다를 더 많이 써요. 이 문형은 글, 노래, 수필에서 써요. 앞에는 보통 '-(으)면'이 오고, 현실은 반대여서 뒤에 '그런데 …'가 이어지기도 해요.
ne: In everyday talk, -(으)면 좋겠다 is more common. This form belongs to writing, songs and essays. It often follows a '-(으)면' clause, and reality is the opposite of the wish.
ex: 길이 막히지 않으면 일찍 도착하련만 오늘은 차가 너무 많아요.
If the road weren't jammed I'd arrive early, but there are so many cars today.
어머니가 살아 계시면 이 집을 보고 기뻐하시련만.
If my mother were alive, she would be so glad to see this house.
I would feel less lonely if a friend were by my side.
If even a word came, I'd feel at ease.
집이 조금만 더 크면 온 가족이 모이련만 방이 하나밖에 없어요.
If the house were a bit bigger the whole family could gather, but there's only one room.
cz: If I had wings, I'd fly to the sea right now.
If Father were healthy, we could travel together.

fe: I practiced hard, yet the result wasn't good.
xk: 앞 일과 다르게 뒤 일이 일어났을 때 써요. '-지만', '-는데도'와 비슷해요. 지난 일은 -았/었건만이에요.
xe: Used when what follows is the opposite of what you'd expect from the first part. Similar to -지만 and -는데도. For past events, use -았/었건만.
nk: 앞 일이 이러면 뒤 일도 이래야 하는데 아니어서 서운하거나 놀라는 느낌이 있어요. 글과 노래에서 많이 써요. -지만은 이런 느낌이 없어요.
ne: There is a feeling of disappointment or surprise: given the first part, the second part should have followed. Common in writing and songs. -지만 carries no such feeling.
ex: Winter is over, yet the wind is still cold.
문은 열려 있건만 안에는 아무도 없었다.
The door was open, yet no one was inside.
엄마는 늘 걱정하셨건만 나는 듣지 않았어요.
Mom always worried, yet I didn't listen.
Old in years, still young at heart.
Seoyeon worked late, yet the pay stayed the same.
cz: I took expensive medicine, yet I didn't get better.
The night had grown late, yet the child didn't fall asleep.

f: V 어간+ㄴ다는/는다는 것이 + 뜻과 다른 결과
fe: I meant to drink water, but I drank juice.
xk: 하려고 한 일과 다른 일이 일어났을 때 써요. 받침이 없는 동사는 '-ㄴ다는 것이', 받침이 있는 동사는 '-는다는 것이' 형태로 써요. 뒤에는 실수한 결과가 와요.
xe: Use it when something different from what you intended happened. Add -ㄴ다는 것이 to a verb without a final consonant, and -는다는 것이 to one with it. The mistaken result comes next.
nk: '그만'이나 '잘못해서'와 자주 써요. 하려던 일을 먼저 말하고 실수를 말해요. 말할 때는 '-ㄴ다는 게 / -는다는 게'로 줄여요.
ne: Often used with '그만' or '잘못해서'. You state the intended act first, then the slip. In speech it shortens to '-ㄴ다는 게 / -는다는 게'.
ex: I meant to put in salt, but I put in sugar.
I meant to call Minsu, but I called Sarah by mistake.
불을 끈다는 것이 그만 라디오를 껐어요.
I meant to turn off the light, but I turned off the radio.
버스를 탄다는 것이 반대 방향 버스를 탔어요.
I meant to take the bus, but I got on the one going the other way.
우산을 챙긴다는 것이 그냥 나와 버렸어요.
I meant to bring an umbrella, but I just walked out without it.
cz: 오븐에 빵을 ___ 그만 태워 버렸어요. (굽다 + -ㄴ/는다는 것이)
I meant to bake bread, but I burned it.
I meant to close the door, but I opened the window.

f: V 어간+(으)려야 (받침 없음 -려야, 받침 있음 -으려야, ㄹ받침 -려야) + 못/-(으)ㄹ 수 없다
fe: However hard I try to hold it in, I can't.
xk: '아무리 하려고 해도 안 돼요'라는 뜻이에요. 동사 어간에 -(으)려야를 붙이고, 뒤에는 안 되는 일을 말해요.
xe: It means 'even if I try to do it, it doesn't work.' Add -(으)려야 to a verb stem, then say what can't be done.
nk: 애써 봐도 결과가 안 되는 상황에서 써요. 뒤에는 '-(으)ㄹ 수 없다', '못', '안 되다' 같은 부정이 와요.
ne: Use it when your effort doesn't get results. A negative usually follows, such as -(으)ㄹ 수 없다, 못, or 안 되다.
ex: 너무 시끄러워서 자려야 잘 수가 없어요.
It's so noisy that I can't sleep however I try.
바빠서 친구를 만나려야 만날 시간이 없어요.
I'm busy, so even if I try to meet my friend, I have no time.
다리가 아파서 일어나려야 일어날 수가 없어요.
My leg hurts, so however I try to stand up, I can't.
여행 중에는 전화를 걸려야 걸 수가 없었어요.
On the trip, I couldn't make a call however I tried.
작은 방이라서 숨으려야 숨을 곳이 없어요.
The room is small, so there's nowhere to hide even if I try.
cz: 비가 너무 많이 와서 밖에 ___ 나갈 수가 없어요. (나가다 + -(으)려야)
It's raining so hard that I can't go out even if I try.
그 노래 이름을 ___ 떠올릴 수가 없어요. (떠올리다 + -(으)려야)
However hard I try to recall that song's name, I can't.

f: V 어간+ㄹ라치면 (받침 있음 -을라치면) + 꼭/번번이 + 뒤따르는 일
fe: Whenever I'm about to clean, a guest always shows up.
xk: '하려고만 하면 꼭'이라는 뜻이에요. 동사 어간에 -(으)ㄹ라치면을 붙이고, 뒤에는 그때마다 생기는 일을 말해요.
xe: It means 'every time I'm about to do something.' Add -(으)ㄹ라치면 to a verb stem, then say what keeps happening.
nk: 뒤에는 보통 방해되는 일, 마음에 안 드는 일이 와요. '꼭', '늘' 같은 말과 자주 함께 써요. 말할 때 쓰는 이해용 표현이고, 한 번만 있었던 일에는 쓰지 않아요.
ne: What follows is usually an annoying or unwelcome event, often with 꼭 or 늘. It is a spoken form for understanding. Don't use it for something that happened only once.
ex: Whenever I'm about to read, my younger sibling talks to me.
Whenever I'm about to rest, the office calls.
Whenever I try to sleep, the next-door neighbor gets noisy.
Whenever I try to take a photo, the child runs away.
Whenever I'm about to start studying for the exam, I get sleepy.
cz: Whenever I'm about to do my homework, my friend asks me to play.
Whenever I'm about to get on the bus, it always leaves.

fk: 친구가 길을 잃을까 봐 같이 갔어요.
fe: I went along with my friend for fear he'd get lost.
xk: '혹시 그렇게 될까 걱정해서'라는 뜻이에요. 어간에 -ㄹ까 봐(받침이 있으면 -을까 봐)를 붙이고, 뒤에 그 걱정 때문에 한 행동을 말해요.
xe: It means 'because I worry it might happen.' Add -ㄹ까 봐 (-을까 봐 after a final consonant), then say what you did because of the worry.
nk: 말할 때 가장 자연스러운 표현이에요. 일어나지 않은 일을 걱정하는 마음이라서, 뒤에는 보통 걱정을 막으려고 한 행동이 와요. 같은 뜻의 글말은 '-(으)ㄹ세라'예요.
ne: This is the natural form in speech. The worry is about something that hasn't happened yet, so the second part is usually an action to prevent it. The written-style equivalent is -(으)ㄹ세라.
ex: I took a taxi because I was afraid of being late.
I brought an umbrella in case it rained.
I didn't tell my friend so he wouldn't worry.
환절기라서 감기에 걸릴까 봐 따뜻하게 입었어요.
It's the change of seasons, so I dressed warmly for fear of catching a cold.
어머니가 혼자 있을까 봐 매일 전화를 드려요.
I call my mother every day so she won't be alone.
cz: I studied all night for fear of failing the exam.
I left home early because I was afraid I'd miss the train.

fk: 어머니는 아들이 길을 잃을세라 손을 꼭 잡았다.
fe: Mother held her son's hand tightly lest he get lost.
xk: '혹시 안 좋은 일이 생길까 봐 걱정해서'라는 뜻이에요. 글이나 편지에서 써요. 어간에 -ㄹ세라(받침이 있으면 -을세라)를 붙여요.
xe: It means 'for fear that something bad might happen.' It belongs to writing and letters. Add -ㄹ세라 (-을세라 after a final consonant) to the stem.
nk: '-(으)ㄹ까 봐'와 뜻은 같지만 글말 느낌이 강해요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '-(으)ㄹ까 봐'를 써요. 뒤에는 걱정을 막으려고 조심하는 행동이 와요.
ne: The meaning is the same as -(으)ㄹ까 봐, but it feels literary. In conversation with friends, use -(으)ㄹ까 봐. The second part is a careful action to prevent the worry.
ex: 지민은 비밀이 들킬세라 문을 꼭 닫았다.
Jimin shut the door tight lest his secret be found out.
서연은 꽃이 시들세라 날마다 물을 주었다.
Seoyeon watered the flowers every day so they wouldn't wilt.
수진은 편지가 젖을세라 가방 깊이 넣었다.
Sujin put the letter deep in her bag lest it get wet.
어머니는 내가 타지에서 굶을세라 반찬을 보냈다.
Mother sent side dishes so I wouldn't go hungry away from home.
마이크는 실수할세라 보고서를 두 번 읽었다.
Mike read the report twice for fear of making a mistake.
cz: Hajun carried the test paper carefully lest it get crumpled.
Yuna opened the door gently so the baby wouldn't be startled.

fe: It's raining, so take an umbrella with you.
xk: 부모나 어른이 아랫사람에게 따뜻하게 말하는 명령이에요. 동사 어간에 '-거라'를 붙여요. '오다'만 '오너라'가 돼요.
xe: A warm command from a parent or elder to someone younger. Add -거라 to a verb stem. Only 오다 becomes 오너라.
nk: 아이나 손아랫사람에게만 써요. 친구나 윗사람에게 쓰면 안 돼요. 요즘 대화에서는 드물고, 편지·옛이야기·드라마에서 자주 들려요. 보통 명령 '-아/어라'보다 부드러워요.
ne: Only used toward children or someone younger, never toward friends or elders. It's rare in daily talk today but common in letters, old tales, and dramas. It sounds softer than the plain command -아/어라.
ex: It's late, so go to bed now.
The road is slippery, so go slowly.
Stay healthy even after you go to Seoul.
If you're sick, don't put up with it; take some medicine.
Listen well to your teacher at school.
cz: When you get home, wash your hands first. (an elder speaking to a child, -거라 form)
You caught a cold, so rest well at home today. (an elder speaking to a child, -거라 form)

fe: I'm doing well here.
xk: 옛 편지나 사극에서 쓰는 말투(하오체)예요. 받침이 없으면 -오, 있으면 -소를 붙여요. 과거는 -았/었소예요. 읽어서 알아보는 말이에요.
xe: This is the old-style speech (hao-che) seen in old letters and historical dramas. Use -오 after a vowel and -소 after a final consonant. Past is -았/었소. You only need to recognize it when reading.
nk: 요즘 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 편지, 사극, 옛 소설에서 만나요. 높임도 낮춤도 아닌 점잖은 어른의 말투예요.
ne: It's almost never used in everyday talk now. You'll meet it in letters, historical dramas, and old novels. It's neither humble nor casual; it sounds like a dignified older speaker.
ex: I was glad to receive your letter.
It has already turned cold here.
I am waiting for news of you.
cz: My dear, I will go home tomorrow. (old letter style, -오/-소)
Being with you, my heart is at ease. (old letter style, -오/-소)

fe: Your handwriting is as lovely as ever, I see.
xk: 새로 알게 된 것을 보고 감탄하는 옛 말투예요. 형용사는 -구려, 동사는 -는구려를 써요. '-군요'와 비슷해요.
xe: An old-style way to show you've just noticed something. Use -구려 with adjectives and -는구려 with verbs. It is like -군요.
nk: 편지나 사극에서 '아, 그렇구나' 하는 느낌으로 써요. 요즘 말로는 '-군요'예요. 읽어서 알아보는 말이에요.
ne: In letters and dramas it carries the feeling of 'oh, I see.' In modern speech it is -군요. You only need to recognize it when reading.
ex: How fast the child is growing!
The sea here is really wide, I see.
Winter has come already, I see.
The rain is finally stopping, I see.
cz: Oh, this house has such a big yard!
Look, the flowers are in full bloom again this year!

f: N+일랑 (모음·받침 뒤에 두루 씀) · 줄여서 N+ㄹ랑(날랑), N+을랑
fe: Don't you worry about it.
xk: 명사 뒤에 붙어서 '그것은'이라는 뜻으로 강조해요. 모음 뒤든 받침 뒤든 '일랑'을 두루 쓰고, 줄여서 'ㄹ랑'(날랑)이나 '을랑'으로도 써요. 뒤에는 '-지 마세요' 같은 말이 자주 와요.
xe: Attach it to a noun to mean 'as for that one', with emphasis. 일랑 is used after both vowels and final consonants, and it can be shortened to ㄹ랑 (날랑) or 을랑. It is often followed by a prohibition like -지 마세요.
nk: '-은/는'보다 말투가 예스럽고 정이 있어요. 그 일은 두고 다른 일을 하라는 느낌이에요. 보통 말이나 편지에서 쓰고, 딱딱한 글에서는 잘 안 써요.
ne: It sounds older and warmer than -은/는. It carries the feeling 'leave that aside and do this other thing'. Used in speech and letters, rarely in stiff writing.
ex: 숙제일랑 나중에 하고 먼저 밥을 먹어요.
Leave the homework for later; eat first.
Leave your bags here and go.
I'll do the dishes, so don't bother.
Don't wait for me; go ahead.
Leave the papers on the desk.
cz: 시험 ___ 신경 쓰지 말고 푹 쉬세요. (결과)
Don't mind the exam result; just rest well. (use 일랑)
I'll do the laundry. Sit and rest. (use 일랑)

fe: If it rains, use an umbrella.
xk: '-거든'에 'ㄹ랑'이 붙은 말이에요. 뜻은 '-거든'과 같아요. 앞일이 생기면 뒤에서 어떻게 하라고 말할 때 써요.
xe: It is -거든 with ㄹ랑 added, and the meaning is the same as -거든. Use it to say what to do if the first thing happens.
nk: 편하고 정다운 입말이에요. 뒤에는 명령·권유가 자주 와요. 글이나 격식 있는 자리에서는 '-(으)면'이 더 자연스러워요.
ne: A friendly spoken form. A command or suggestion usually follows. In writing or formal settings, -(으)면 is more natural.
ex: Call me when you get home.
배가 고프거들랑 냉장고에서 빵을 꺼내 먹어.
If you're hungry, take bread from the fridge.
If you have time, come to our shop.
If a guest comes, serve tea.
When your homework is done, tell me.
cz: If you are going to be late for the meeting, contact us in advance. (use -거들랑)
If the road is jammed, take a taxi. (use -거들랑)

f: N+일랑은 (모음·받침 뒤에 두루 씀) · 줄여서 N+ㄹ랑은, N+을랑은
fe: Please don't bring a gift.
xk: 명사 뒤에 붙어서 '그것은'이라고 짚어 말해요. 뒤에는 안 하는 일이나 금지하는 말이 자주 와요.
xe: Attach it to a noun to pick it out: 'as for that one'. A negative or prohibition often follows.
nk: '-일랑'에 '은'이 더 붙어서 '그것은 따로 두고'라는 뜻이 더 분명해요. 그 일은 빼고 다른 일을 하자는 느낌이에요. 예스럽고 정다운 말투예요.
ne: Adding 은 to -일랑 makes the 'set that aside' sense clearer. It suggests leaving that out and doing something else. The tone is old-fashioned and warm.
ex: You don't have to go to tomorrow's meeting.
어려운 말일랑은 쓰지 않고 쉽게 말해요.
Skip the hard words and speak simply.
휴대폰일랑은 가방에 넣어 두고 수업을 들어요.
Put your phone in your bag and listen to class.
Leave the homework for later and rest first.
널랑은 집에 두고 나 혼자 갔어.
I left you at home and went alone.
cz: ___ 서랍에 넣고 다른 건 그냥 두세요. (양말)
As for the socks, put them in the drawer and leave the rest alone. (use 일랑은)
Leave studying for tomorrow and rest today. (use 일랑은)

fk: 저는 시험 결과를 기다리면서 가슴을 졸였어요.
fe: I was on tenterhooks while I waited for my test result.
xk: 걱정이 돼서 마음이 편하지 않을 때 써요. 결과가 나오기 전에 불안한 마음을 말해요. '졸이다'를 써요. '졸리다'가 아니에요.
xe: Use it when you are worried and cannot relax. It describes anxious waiting before a result. The verb is 졸이다, not 졸리다.
nk: 합격 발표, 수술, 경기처럼 결과를 기다리는 일에 자주 써요. 일이 끝난 뒤에는 '마음이 놓이다'를 써요. '걱정하다'보다 가슴이 조마조마한 느낌이 더 커요.
ne: Often used for waiting on exam results, surgery, or a match. Once it is over, you switch to 마음이 놓이다. It feels more tense and nervous than plain 걱정하다 (to worry).
ex: 아이가 밤늦게까지 돌아오지 않아서 부모님은 가슴을 졸였어요.
The child did not come home until late at night, so the parents were on edge.
비행기가 흔들릴 때 승객들은 모두 가슴을 졸였어요.
When the plane shook, all the passengers held their breath in fear.
경기를 보는 내내 팬들은 가슴을 졸이며 지켜봤어요.
The fans watched on the edge of their seats all through the match.
수술이 끝나기 전에 가족은 가슴을 졸이고 있었어요.
Before the surgery was over, the family was waiting anxiously.
합격 소식을 듣기 전에 사라는 가슴을 졸였어요.
Before she heard the news that she passed, Sara was on pins and needles.
cz: The announcement is late, so everyone is on edge right now.
아이가 열이 나서 엄마는 밤새___ (가슴을 졸이다).
The child had a fever, so the mother was anxious all night.

fe: The child got home, so I felt relieved.
xk: 걱정이 사라져서 편안해질 때 써요. 걱정하던 일이 잘 끝나거나 믿을 사람이 있을 때 말해요.
xe: Use it when worry goes away and you feel at ease. It is for when a worrying thing ends well, or when someone reliable is there.
nk: 먼저 걱정이 있었고, 그 걱정이 풀렸을 때 써요. 걱정이 없었던 때는 잘 안 써요. '안심하다'와 뜻이 비슷하지만, '마음이 놓이다'는 마음이 저절로 편해지는 느낌이에요.
ne: There must be worry first, then it is resolved. It is not natural when you had no worry. It is close to 안심하다, but the feeling here comes by itself, as a weight lifts from the heart.
ex: I feel at ease because my friend is next to me.
시험 결과가 걱정됐는데 합격해서 마음이 놓였어요.
I was worried about the test result, but I passed, so I felt relieved.
의사 선생님이 괜찮다고 해서 마음이 놓였어요.
The doctor said I was fine, so I felt reassured.
여행 짐을 다 챙겨서 마음이 놓여요.
I packed all my travel bags, so I feel at ease.
하준이 같이 가면 마음이 놓일 거예요.
If Hajun goes with us, I will feel at ease.
cz: The rain stopped, so now I feel relieved.
The interview was over, so Jimin felt relieved.
